name: Vienna
summary: Austria's imperial capital: palaces, concert halls, coffee houses and wine taverns at the edge of the city.

name: Tyrol
summary: High Alpine valleys around Innsbruck, known for skiing in winter and hiking in summer.

name: Région de Bruxelles-Capitale/ Brussels Hoofdstedelijk Gewest
Lake Geneva region
summary: Geneva, Lausanne and Montreux on the lake, with terraced vineyards and the Alps of Valais behind.

name: Central Switzerland
summary: Lucerne and its lake surrounded by classic Swiss peaks such as Pilatus, Rigi and Titlis.

name: Cyprus
summary: A warm island with long beach seasons, Roman mosaics, painted mountain churches and the Troodos range.

name: Prague
summary: A compact capital of Gothic and baroque streets, a hilltop castle and a long beer tradition.

name: Upper Bavaria
summary: Munich, clear lakes and the Bavarian Alps, with castles and beer gardens along the way.

name: Berlin
summary: Germany's capital: twentieth-century history, a large museum scene and famous nightlife.

name: Copenhagen region
summary: Denmark's capital region: harbour baths, design, cycling everywhere and castles along the coast.

name: Estonia
summary: Tallinn's medieval old town, with forests, bogs and quiet Baltic islands beyond it.

name: Attica
summary: Athens and its coast: the Acropolis, world-class museums and beaches along the Athens Riviera.

name: South Aegean
summary: The Cyclades and Dodecanese: Santorini, Mykonos, Rhodes and dozens of smaller islands.

name: Crete
summary: Greece's largest island: Minoan palaces, mountain villages, deep gorges and clear water.
highlights: Beaches such as Elafonisi and Balos

name: Catalonia
summary: Barcelona's architecture and beaches, the rocky Costa Brava and the Pyrenees within a few hours of each other.

name: Balearic Islands
summary: Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza and Formentera: clear water, small coves and busy summers.

name: Andalusia
summary: Moorish palaces, flamenco and very hot summers, with beaches on both the Mediterranean and the Atlantic and the Sierra Nevada inland.
highlights: Costa del Sol and Costa de la Luz beaches

name: North and East Finland
summary: Lapland and the lake country: forests, northern lights in winter and midnight sun in summer.

name: Ile-de-France
summary: Paris and its surroundings: museums, monuments, cafe life and royal palaces such as Versailles.

name: Brittany
summary: A wild Atlantic coast of lighthouses and granite, with standing stones, walled ports and a strong Celtic identity.

name: Rhone-Alpes
summary: Lyon's food scene and the French Alps, including Mont Blanc and many of Europe's largest ski areas.

name: Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur
summary: Lavender fields, Roman towns and the French Riviera, rising quickly to the southern Alps.
highlights: Roman sites in Arles and Orange

name: Adriatic Croatia
summary: The Dalmatian coast and Istria: walled cities, over a thousand islands and national parks with lakes and waterfalls.
highlights: Old towns of Dubrovnik and Split

name: Budapest
summary: Hungary's capital on the Danube, known for thermal baths, grand nineteenth-century buildings and ruin bars.

name: Northern and Western Ireland
summary: Ireland's Atlantic edge: Galway, Connemara, Donegal and long stretches of empty coast.

name: Iceland
summary: Volcanoes, glaciers, waterfalls and geothermal pools on a cool, windy island.

name: Campania
summary: Naples, Vesuvius and the Amalfi Coast: Roman ruins, cliffside villages and some of Italy's best-loved food.
highlights: Amalfi Coast drives and boat trips

name: Apulia
summary: The heel of Italy: whitewashed towns, olive groves and a long coastline on both the Adriatic and Ionian seas.

name: Sicily
summary: The largest Mediterranean island, with Greek temples, baroque towns, long beaches and Mount Etna above them all.

name: Veneto
summary: Venice and its lagoon, Verona, Lake Garda's eastern shore and the Dolomites to the north.

name: Tuscany
summary: Rolling vineyard hills, walled medieval towns and the Renaissance art of Florence, with a quieter coast on the Tyrrhenian Sea.
highlights: Hill towns such as Siena and San Gimignano

name: Lazio
summary: Rome and its countryside: ancient ruins, baroque squares and Vatican City, with volcanic lakes and beaches a short train ride away.
highlights: Day trips to Tivoli and Ostia

name: Montenegro
summary: A small country of steep mountains and a short Adriatic coast, with the fjord-like Bay of Kotor.
highlights: Old towns of Kotor and Budva

name: Malta
summary: Three small islands with fortified harbours, prehistoric temples and clear water for diving.

name: North Holland
summary: Amsterdam's canals and museums, with windmills, tulip fields and North Sea beaches nearby.

name: Western Norway
summary: The fjords: steep walls, waterfalls and glaciers, with Bergen as the gateway. Expect rain in any month.

name: Lesser Poland
summary: Krakow's medieval centre and the Tatra mountains around Zakopane to the south.

name: Northern Portugal
summary: Porto, the terraced vineyards of the Douro valley and green, rainy mountains towards Spain.

name: Algarve
summary: Portugal's sunny south coast: golden cliffs, sea caves and long sandy beaches on the Atlantic.

name: Lisbon
summary: Portugal's hilly capital on the Tagus, with tiled streets, old trams and Atlantic beaches close by.

name: Stockholm
summary: A capital spread over islands, with a medieval old town and an archipelago of thousands more islands.

name: Istanbul
summary: A huge city across two continents, with Byzantine and Ottoman monuments, bazaars and the Bosphorus.
highlights: Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque
Food from street stalls to meyhanes

name: Aegean coast of Turkey (Mugla and Aydin)
summary: Bodrum, Marmaris and Fethiye on the coast, with Pamukkale's white terraces and Greek and Roman ruins inland.

name: Antalya
summary: The Turkish Riviera: long hot summers, turquoise water, ancient cities and the Taurus mountains behind the coast.
highlights: Ancient cities such as Perge and Aspendos

name: Cappadocia
summary: A high plateau of rock chimneys, cave churches and underground cities in central Turkey.

name: Trabzon, Ordu, Giresun, Rize, Artvin, Gümüşhane
Inner London West
summary: Central London: Westminster, royal parks, free national museums and West End theatre.

name: Outer London — East and North East
Outer London — West and North West
Scottish Highlands and Islands
summary: Mountains, lochs and remote islands, with castles, whisky distilleries and very few people.
